blocks.text: tried. Bhīma fulfils his first Pratijñā, and kills Duḥśāsana in battle, without conflicting Dharma. Towards the end of the war, the Kaurava army was reduced to Duryodhana, Ashwatthāma, Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarma. When Duryodhana was given the option to choose any one of the Pāṇḍava warriors for a one-on-one battle, he picked Bhīma and suggested a mace fight. The fight continued for a long time and Bhīma started getting tired. Observing this, Kṛṣṇa signalled Bhīma to strike Duryodhana hard on his thigh and break it. Bhīma followed Bhagavān's instructions and defeated Duryodhana. Here we see that Bhīma chose to fight and defeat Duryodhana in full adherence to dharma. His Pratijñā to break Duryodhana's thigh does not interfere with his dharmic acumen. When he did break his thigh in the end, it was only to fulfil Bhagavān's instruction and not his Pratijñā. Though Bhīma ended up making Pratijñā's out of anger, he did not let it cloud his judgement or his decisions.

All three Pratijñās were emotionally based. Gāndhārī's Pratijñā, though considered noble, blinded her to the adharma of her children. This adharma grew day by day and eventually resulted in the bloodshed of the entire family alongside countless others. Arjuna's Pratijñā could have gotten him in a fix since he took the vow without any forethought. But thanks to Kṛṣṇa he could fulfil it.
